blocks.content: While the Finance Commission is a constitutional body mandated to recommend fiscal devolution, NITI Aayog acts as a non-constitutional think tank driving cooperative federalism.

rows: Policy think tank providing strategic advice
No power to allocate central financial funds
Constituted every 5 years by the President

items: Article 280 mandates the constitution of the Finance Commission by the President every fifth year or earlier.
NITI Aayog lacks fund allocation powers; fiscal transfers are handled via the Finance Commission and the Ministry of Finance.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body created under Article 280 of the Constitution to advise on tax revenue distribution between the Centre and States.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on January 1, 2015, functioning as an extra-constitutional, non-statutory executive policy think tank.
Unlike the former Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not possess powers to allocate central funds to state governments or ministries.
The Finance Commission submits its fiscal recommendations directly to the President of India every five years.
NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism through a bottom-up approach, featuring a Governing Council comprising all state Chief Ministers and UT Lt. Governors.
